$meta.name: vinc-design
$meta.note: The source of truth for the Vinc 'Signal' design system. base = the homepage and web Vinc theme (Home · Signal); tenants/desktop = the desktop application (Deep Signal). Operated dark first: the runtime default is data-theme=dark, while the engine is light-first and emits :root=light, so the consuming shell pins dark itself. Derivation: imports/figma-variables-2026-07-19.json (mapped by hand from Figma). The state notation (●◐○·≡≈) is kept alongside colour, never instead of it. Glow is for graph nodes only.
$meta.a11y: WCAG 2.2 AA. Only tokens verified at a body contrast of 4.5:1 or better may be used as text.

atlasScene.note: Depth tiers for the Atlas 3D mark, used only by the dark glow branch (app/src/surfaces/atlas3d.ts). This is the canonical copy; imports/figma-variables-*.json is only the record of the original import. Just three keys are consumed: fill, stroke and glowOpacity. glowRadius, edge and grid were removed on 2026-08-02 because no code read them (they were dead handles: changing the value changed nothing on screen). Verified by Vinc/scripts/gate_contrast.py

domainTint.note: Open-layer domain tint for the Atlas marks (off by default). This is emphasis, not encoding: it is a user toggle in AtlasPrefs, so it must never be the only way to tell two nodes apart. The hue comes from a hash of the topic string, so a topic keeps its hue no matter which other topics are on screen, and collisions are possible and tolerated. Saturation and lightness are fixed here rather than in app code so the contrast floor is a token, not a literal: the lightness is chosen to sit near the ink it replaces, which is what keeps the tinted mark readable in each mode. Consumed by app/src/atlas-tint.ts.

grain_50.$description: Light card surface, the top of the grain ramp

grain_100.$description: Light page background (the grain grey of the logo reference) · text on a CTA

grain_200.$description: Light alternating section band · muted surface

ink_900.$description: Cool near-black ink, body text in light mode. Pure black is forbidden

ink_400.$description: Captions and meta only (light). Forbidden for body text (the caption layer)

indigo_900.$description: The indigo of the logo tip. Light CTA surface · the constant CTA band

indigo_700.$description: Dark CTA surface · active fill (the application's accent/deep)

indigo_600.$description: Light link and info (AA ✓ on grain)

peri_400.$description: Periwinkle. The focus ring in both modes · dark link · the source colour of the graph glow

peri_200.$description: Periwinkle, lightened. Dark CTA text · active emphasis

peri_250.$description: The end of the logo tip gradient (dark), one step brighter than peri_200. The body of the mark is currentColor and only the tip falls to this colour

warn_bg.$description: Light warning background and chip only. Forbidden as text

win_close.$description: Hover on the titlebar close button. This is an operating-system convention (Windows), not a brand colour, so it does not change with the mode and sits on a different axis from danger: danger states a condition, this follows a window-control convention. The counterpart of the Figma Window collection (223:35)

d_bg0.$description: Dark page and application background, the deepest layer (Deep Signal)

d_bg1.$description: Dark surface · alternating section · panel base

d_bg2.$description: Dark card · left navigation · raised surface

d_mute.$description: Dark caption · meta · disabled. Forbidden for body text

d_warn_bg.$description: Dark warning background only. Forbidden as text

grain_300.$description: The floor for the light fade channel, APCA Lc 16.0. hairline (Lc 9.3) falls below the invisibility floor of 15, so it cannot be the faded colour of a graph line

peri_500.$description: Cross-domain edge in light mode: peri_400 darkened until it reaches WCAG 3:1 (2.49 → 3.00). In light mode WCAG is the stricter of the two measures

slate_400.$description: Dark node ring and cross edge, APCA Lc 45.9. A thin line is held to the fine-detail threshold (Lc 45), not the solid one (Lc 30)

slate_500.$description: The main edge line. Dark Lc 30.9 / 4.42:1 · light Lc 62.6 / 3.92:1, the **neutral that passes both gates in both modes**

slate_700.$description: The floor for the dark fade channel, just above the APCA invisibility floor of Lc 15 (15.9). The fade channel is exempt from 3:1 but must never disappear entirely
